description: We are Team kyber, a passionate group of space enthusiasts, data explorers, and AI builders participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge! Focused on the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge, our mission is to leverage data analysis, astrophysics, and machine learning to uncover hidden signals in cosmic datasets and explore the frontiers of our solar system and beyond. We welcome fellow data lovers and space dreamers to collaborate with us!
summary:
SPHEREx Sky Explorer is an interactive website that helps students and curious people explore real infrared images of space and see how the sky changes over time. It addresses a simple problem: NASA makes astronomy data publicly available, but understanding and comparing it often requires specialist software and scientific knowledge.

Our platform lets users search for an object or enter sky coordinates, view available SPHEREx observations, and compare images taken on different dates. They can place images side by side, move a divider between them, or rapidly switch between observations. The website checks whether images are suitable for subtraction and explains why an apparent difference may need further investigation.

A documented investigation compares two real SPHEREx observations near Barnard’s Star. It shows how changing foreground light can make a field appear dimmer without proving that a star faded or moved.

Users can also inspect available infrared measurements, follow guided learning missions, and save notes in a personal journal. Persistent caching reduces repeated downloads. By connecting real observations with simple explanations, SPHEREx Sky Explorer helps people move from looking at space to asking and investigating scientific questions.
details:
SPHEREx Sky Explorer is a public web tool for exploring how the infrared sky changes over time. Users can view real SPHEREx observations, compare dates using blink, swipe, side-by-side, and difference modes, and record their findings.

The platform explains that visible changes may come from object motion, brightness changes, foreground light, alignment, wavelength differences, or missing data. This helps beginners investigate evidence without making false conclusions.

We built it with React, TypeScript, Vite, Python, FastAPI, Astropy, NumPy, FITS/WCS tools, and NASA/IPAC IRSA data. Persistent caching improves loading speed.

Its main benefit is making real NASA observations understandable and interactive for students and the public while maintaining scientific accuracy, accessibility, and clear data provenance.
